headline: The periodic Airy group has an exact all-rational-time cubic-DFT revival atlas, a minimal full-space period, and complete sampled fixed-mode and finite-support period laws.
nonclaims: a nonlinear KdV theorem or classification of nonperiodic Airy boundary conditions
closed formulas for every cubic Gauss sum at every modulus
compactness, trace class, or an infinite-dimensional Fredholm determinant for U(t)
an arithmetic Euler product, target divisor, counting law, or functional equation
a Hilbert--Polya operator, target zero match, or Route-B input
literature priority for the classical periodic revival identity

receipts.finite_receipt_boundary: Finite modular and DFT rows verify conventions; the all-time Hilbert-space theorem is proof-driven.

route_a.strongest_failure: There is no intrinsic arithmetic owner, rational-prime primitive-orbit dictionary, target determinant, or target global analytic structure.
route_a.strongest_positive: A canonical self-adjoint cubic Fourier generator controls the exact unitary group and every rational Talbot strobe.

theorem.fixed_modes: Its fixed subspace is the closed span of e_n with q dividing n^3, equivalently L(q) divides n where L(q)=product ell^ceil(v_ell(q)/3).
theorem.irrational_sampling: If t/(2*pi) is irrational, the fixed subspace of U(t) consists exactly of constants.
theorem.minimal_full_period: U(t)=I on all L^2(T) exactly for t in 2*pi*Z; hence the least positive full-space period is 2*pi.
theorem.operator_boundary: Every U(t) is unitary but noncompact on infinite-dimensional L^2(T), so it is neither trace class nor a target Fredholm determinant input.
theorem.rational_revival: For gcd(p,q)=1, U(2*pi*p/q)=sum_{r=0}^{q-1} A_r tau_{2*pi*r/q}, where A_r=q^{-1} sum_s exp(2*pi*i*(p*s^3-s*r)/q).
theorem.state_period: A state with nonzero finite Fourier support S has least positive continuous period 2*pi/gcd{|n|^3:n in S}; constants are fixed for every time.
theorem.strobe_order: The rational strobe U(2*pi*p/q) has exact global order q.
theorem.unitary_group: U(t) is a strongly continuous unitary group with self-adjoint Fourier generator D^3, D=-i*d/dx.
